title: Ferrari SF90 vs McLaren Artura: The Difference Nobody Explains
description:
Two plug-in hybrid supercars. Both arrived in the same era, both have a battery of under eight kilowatt hours, both can drive on electricity alone, and both have thrown away the reverse gear. The Ferrari SF90 Stradale and the McLaren Artura look like the same idea. But one costs about twice as much as the other, and the reason is the difference nobody explains. On paper, the SF90 has almost one thousand horsepower and all-wheel drive. The Artura has about six hundred eighty, a V6, and rear-wheel drive. So the easy answer is that the Ferrari is simply more car. But that answer misses the real story, which is about what each company was trying to build, and what each one risked.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
